subject: Discovery recap — propose tri-zone daisychain demo cadence
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Tim Evans <tim.evans@aurelia.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — propose tri-zone daisychain demo cadence

Hi Tim / Hannah — thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next step so we can lock the technical deep dive: 

1) Key takeaways from discovery
- Primary workload: low-latency customer-facing recommendations (multi-tenant), ingesting session context and proprietary embeddings.
- Top constraints: PII segmentation, SOC2 evidence, and tight 99th percentile latency targets for peak traffic.
- Success metric for pilot: end-to-end latency < 350ms median on 8k token context with <= 1.5x cost uplift vs baseline, and clear audit logs.

2) Suggested next meeting: 60-minute technical deep dive (product + infra + security) to validate integration points, network/BYOK requirements, and a short runbook for a 2-week pilot.

3) Scheduling ask (tri-zone cadence)
You mentioned primary participants are split across US (Tim), EU (Hannah), and APAC (engineering on call). To make recurring deep dives feasible, I propose a rotating "daisychain" schedule where each week the meeting favors one region's core working hours and the other regions join at reasonable overlap. That keeps the burden balanced and ensures your engineers can attend at least part of sessions.

Proposed rotation (prefers 60-minute slot):
- Week A (US-friendly): 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 BST
- Week B (EU-friendly): 14:00 BST / 09:00 ET / 22:00 SGT
- Week C (APAC-friendly): 07:00 PT / 16:00 SGT / 19:00 AEST

I attached a one-pager with the MVP requirements and an .ics that maps the rotation to your local times. If that approach works, please: 1) flag preferred weeks for the first three meetings, or 2) pick a single slot from my Calendly (link below) and I’ll set up the recurring series with the proposed rotation.

Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/mina-aurelia-demo
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/s/aur-mvp-reqs

Next steps I’ll take after you confirm: draft mutual action plan, invite Solutions (Karthik) and to capture network/security asks, and reserve a dedicated test GPU for the pilot window.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

Attachments: Aurelia-MVP-requirements.pdf (summary), proposed-daisychain-rotations.ics (calendar template)

From: Tim Evans <tim.evans@aurelia.co>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Li <hannah.li@aurelia.co>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — propose tri-zone daisychain demo cadence

Hey Mina — thanks for the clear write-up and the proposal. That rotation model looks promising — we like the idea of sharing the burden rather than always pushing to US hours. A few notes from our side: 

- We’ll need to include one of our infra engineers (APAC) on the technical deep dive; they are only available late APAC time (18:00–22:00 SGT) most weekdays.
- SOC2 + KMS integration is a hard blocker for legal; Hannah will own the questionnaire and coordinate with your security team.
- For the first session, our preference is to do an EU-friendly slot so Hannah can lead the data/security portion and the APAC engineer can join at the tail end.

Can we aim for the EU-friendly option in your rotation for the first meeting? If so, week of Sep 6 works for us — suggested time: 14:00 BST on Tue Sep 8. If Mina can lock Karthik and Ben for that date I’ll confirm the APAC engineer availability.

—Tim
Tim Evans
Head of Platform | Aurelia Systems
tim.evans@aurelia.co | +44 20 7946 0123

Thanks Tim — Mina flagged this to me. I can cover the US-facing sessions and rotate on the others. Karthik, can you take lead on the EU-friendly session and bring a short checklist for network/firewall requirements?

For Sep 8 at 14:00 BST (Tue) I’m available at 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET — I’ll block my calendar if Tim confirms. Karthik, if you can confirm availability for Sep 8 and whether you need any pre-call artifacts (logs, sample payloads), I’ll send the invite.

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — propose tri-zone daisychain demo cadence

Perfect — I’ll lock Sep 8, 14:00 BST (09:00 PT / 12:00 ET) as the first technical deep dive.

Action items: 
- Mina: create recurring series following the daisychain rotation (Week A US-friendly / Week B EU-friendly / Week C APAC-friendly). I’ll include the .ics rotation file and a short agenda (30m demo, 20m integration questions, 10m pilot runbook).
- Ben: lead the session and intro to Solutions; bring pricing guardrails for pilot.
- Karthik: share a short network checklist and confirm whether you need sample payloads (I attached MVP requirements).
- Tim/Hannah: confirm the APAC engineer name/email and whether they prefer Webex or Zoom.

If anyone objects to the cadence or needs a fixed series instead of a rotation, say so in the next 24 hours — otherwise I’ll send the invite and calendar series invite by EOD.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Mina Haddad
